record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: Let T:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] be an Archimedean t-norm, and let its associated negation be N_T(x)=sup{t in [0,1] : T(x,t)=0}. Assume N_T is involutive, meaning N_T(N_T(x))=x for every x in [0,1]. Must such a t-norm T be conditionally cancellative or left-continuous, or can there exist an Archimedean t-norm with involutive associated negation that fails both of those properties?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 (B. Jayaram). Does there exist any Archimedean t-norm T , whose NT is involutive but is not conditionally cancellative or left-continuous? In other words, is an Archimedean t-norm T whose NT is involutive necessarily conditionally cancellative or left-continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm (t-norm) is a binary operation $T:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ that is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies $T(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$. A t-norm $T$ is called Archimedean if for every $x,y\in(0,1)$ there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $x_T^{(n)}<y$, where $x_T^{(n)}$ denotes the $n$-fold $T$-power of $x$. The associated (natural) negation of $T$ is the map $N_T:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ defined by $N_T(x)=\sup\{t\in[0,1]:T(x,t)=0\}$. The negation $N_T$ is called involutive (strong) if $N_T(N_T(x))=x$ for every $x\in[0,1]$. The t-norm $T$ is said to be conditionally cancellative if $T(x,y)=T(x,z)>0$ implies $y=z$, and left-continuous if it is left-continuous in each argument.

Question: Does there exist an Archimedean t-norm $T$ whose associated negation $N_T$ is involutive but which is neither conditionally cancellative nor left-continuous? Equivalently, must every Archimedean t-norm with involutive associated negation be conditionally cancellative or left-continuous?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work indicates that an Archimedean t-norm whose associated (natural) negation is involutive (strong) must be both conditionally cancellative and left-continuous; the question posed by Jayaram has been answered in the affirmative direction (no such counterexample exists). Results characterizing conditionally cancellative t-subnorms with strong natural negations as t-norms (solving a related problem of U. Höhle) and Jenei's results on left-continuous t-subnorms with involutive negations together resolve the problem.

status_evidence.title: Solution to an open problem: a characterization of conditionally cancellative t-subnorms
status_evidence.snippet: Conditionally cancellative t-subnorms whose natural negations are strong are, in fact, t-norms.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes that strong natural negation forces t-norm structure under conditional cancellativity, contributing to the resolution of Jayaram's question.

status_evidence.title: On an Open Problem of U. Höhle — A Characterization of Conditionally Cancellative T-Subnorms
status_evidence.snippet: Some classes of t-subnorms whose associated negations are involutive become t-norms; Jenei showed it for left-continuous t-subnorms, while Jayaram did the same for conditionally cancellative t-subnorms.
status_evidence.claim: Combined Jenei–Jayaram results show that Archimedean t-norms with involutive associated negation fall into the conditionally cancellative or left-continuous categories.
